title: Reported Speech: Statements and Backshift
summary: Report what another person said by changing direct statements into reported statements. Use natural past-tense backshift, adjust pronouns and references, and recognise when a past event may remain past simple or move to past perfect.
learningObjectives: Turn direct statements into reported statements with said (that) or told someone (that).
Backshift present simple, present continuous, present perfect and common modals after a past reporting verb.
Change first- and second-person pronouns to preserve who said or heard the original words.
Recognise the two common ways of reporting a past-simple event and avoid changing the original meaning.

explanation.heading: Quote directly or report the message
explanation.body: Direct speech reproduces someone’s words; reported speech gives the same message from a later speaker’s point of view. Put a reporting clause such as Maya said before a that-clause. That is often optional in ordinary statements. Use quotation marks for actual direct quotations, not for normal reported clauses.
explanation.example: Direct: “I need more time.” Reported: Maya said that she needed more time.

explanation.heading: Backshift present forms after a past reporting verb
explanation.body: When you tell someone later what was said, verbs commonly shift back one tense: am/is becomes was, are becomes were, present simple becomes past simple, and present continuous becomes past continuous. This makes it clear that the sentence is a report of earlier speech, not a new quotation.
explanation.example: “We work on Saturdays.” → The staff said they worked on Saturdays.

explanation.heading: Report earlier experiences with the past perfect
explanation.body: A present perfect in the original statement commonly becomes a past perfect in later reported speech. Keep the original sequence of events clear: a completed action that was already in the past at the time of speaking remains earlier than the reporting moment.
explanation.example: “I have sent the invoice.” → Leah said she had sent the invoice.

explanation.heading: Backshift common modals
explanation.body: After a past reporting verb, will commonly becomes would and can becomes could. Do not add to before the verb after would or could. A negative carries across as would not or could not. Use the modal that preserves the original promise, prediction, ability or possibility.
explanation.example: “I will bring the key.” → Karim said he would bring the key.

explanation.heading: Adjust people and references
explanation.body: Change I, we, my, our and you when the person reporting is not the original speaker or listener. The correct pronoun depends on who spoke, who was addressed and who is retelling the message. Time or place expressions may also change when the reporting situation changes; keep an expression unchanged if it still fits.
explanation.example: Tariq told Emma, “I can lend you my notes.” → Emma said Tariq could lend her his notes.

explanation.heading: Report a past simple event in two possible ways
explanation.body: When the original statement uses the past simple, reported speech may keep that past simple or use the past perfect. Both forms can be appropriate when the context and event sequence are clear. Do not automatically treat every unchanged past-simple verb as wrong.
explanation.example: “I met my tutor yesterday.” → Nina said she met her tutor yesterday; she also could have said she had met her tutor yesterday.

comparisons.title: Direct words and a later report

left.label: Direct quotation
left.example: “I am reviewing the contract,” Rosa said.
left.note: These are Rosa’s own words at the time.

right.label: Reported statement
right.example: Rosa said that she was reviewing the contract.
right.note: The later report adjusts both speaker and tense.

left.label: At the time of speaking
left.example: “We have finished the survey,” the students said.
left.note: Have finished is present perfect in the original utterance.

right.label: In the later report
right.example: The students said they had finished the survey.
right.note: Had finished makes the earlier completion clear.

comparisons.title: An earlier past event, two reporting choices

left.label: Past simple retained
left.example: Dara said she missed the train on Monday.
left.note: A past simple event can remain in the past simple.

right.label: Past perfect backshift
right.example: Dara said she had missed the train on Monday.
right.note: The past perfect explicitly positions the event before the report.

examples.sentence: The supervisor said the replacement part was in the storeroom.
examples.note: Is becomes was when the report adopts the normal past reporting viewpoint.

examples.sentence: Kelsey told her colleague that she was preparing the slides.
examples.note: Present continuous in direct speech commonly becomes past continuous.

examples.sentence: The visitors said they had already booked their tickets.
examples.note: Had booked reports an earlier completed booking.

examples.sentence: Milo said he could stay until Friday.
examples.note: Could is the backshifted form of can.

examples.sentence: Alina said that she would send her brother the directions.
examples.note: Would keeps the promise from an original will-statement.

examples.sentence: Hannah said she lost her badge on Tuesday.
examples.note: The past-simple event can remain past simple.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Olivia said she is taking the exam that afternoon.
commonMistakes.correct: Olivia said she was taking the exam that afternoon.
commonMistakes.why: In a report explicitly using past-time backshift, present continuous becomes past continuous.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Jon said he has finished the design before the meeting.
commonMistakes.correct: Jon said he had finished the design before the meeting.
commonMistakes.why: A reported earlier completion normally uses had + past participle in this backshifted context.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The driver said he will arrive before noon.
commonMistakes.correct: The driver said he would arrive before noon.
commonMistakes.why: In a backshifted report, will becomes would.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Lara told that she needed a taxi.
commonMistakes.correct: Lara said that she needed a taxi.
commonMistakes.why: Tell needs an object naming the person addressed in this construction; said that introduces a statement without an object.

studyTips: Underline the reporting verb and identify who originally said I, we or you before changing any pronouns.
Make a two-column verb map: am/is → was, have/has done → had done, will → would, can → could; practise one original statement for each.
When the original sentence is already past simple, test both retained past simple and past perfect before deciding what fits the story.

exercises.prompt: At 9 a.m. Lucas said, “I am waiting outside.” At noon his sister reported: Lucas said he ___ outside. Use normal past-time backshift.
exercises.feedback: Am waiting normally becomes was waiting in a later report with said.

exercises.prompt: Yesterday Faye said, “I have lost the receipt.” Later we reported: Faye said she ___ the receipt.
exercises.feedback: The original present perfect have lost commonly backshifts to had lost.

exercises.prompt: Noah told us, “I will email the drawings.” We reported: Noah said he ___ the drawings.
exercises.feedback: Will commonly changes to would when reporting an earlier statement.

exercises.prompt: Tessa said, “I can use the new scanner.” Later, a teammate reported: Tessa said she ___ the new scanner.
exercises.feedback: Can becomes could, followed by the base form use.

exercises.prompt: Zoe said, “My sister works from home.” Report this with past-time backshift: Zoe said her sister ___ from home. (work)
acceptedAnswers: worked
exercises.feedback: Present simple works commonly becomes past simple worked after said.

exercises.prompt: Evan said, “We are planning a visit.” Report the verb phrase using past continuous: Evan said they ___ a visit. (plan)
acceptedAnswers: were planning
exercises.feedback: We are planning becomes they were planning when the people are reported from an outside viewpoint.

exercises.prompt: Dina said, “I have spoken to the manager.” Complete the backshifted report: Dina said she ___ to the manager. (speak)
acceptedAnswers: had spoken
exercises.feedback: Have spoken becomes had spoken when the report puts the completed event earlier.

exercises.prompt: Avi said, “I will help you tomorrow.” You were the listener. Complete the backshifted report: Avi said he ___ me the next day. (help)
acceptedAnswers: would help
exercises.feedback: Would help reports will help; me names the original listener and the next day replaces tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Bela said she is learning Spanish at that time.
acceptedAnswers: Bela said she was learning Spanish at that time.
exercises.feedback: Use was learning for a past-time report of an ongoing activity.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Gabe said he has already posted the forms before he left.
acceptedAnswers: Gabe said he had already posted the forms before he left.
exercises.feedback: The action was already completed before he left, so the backshifted perfect is had posted.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The guests said they will stay until Sunday, but their visit ended last month.
acceptedAnswers: The guests said they would stay until Sunday, but their visit ended last month.
exercises.feedback: The plan belongs to a finished visit, so would reports the earlier prediction instead of presenting it as still future.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Mia told that she could repair the lamp.
acceptedAnswers: Mia said that she could repair the lamp.
exercises.feedback: Tell needs a listener object; say can introduce a that-clause without one.

speakingExercises.prompt: On Monday, Priya said, “I live near the park.” On Tuesday, report it with Priya as the subject. Use said and backshift live to the past.
acceptedAnswers: Priya said she lived near the park.
Priya said that she lived near the park.
speakingExercises.feedback: In the report, I becomes she and live becomes lived.

speakingExercises.prompt: Yesterday, Theo said, “I am working late.” Report what Theo said, using he and the past continuous. Start with “Theo said”.
acceptedAnswers: Theo said he was working late.
Theo said that he was working late.
speakingExercises.feedback: Was working reports an earlier action that was underway.

speakingExercises.prompt: Sara said, “I have completed the course.” Report this with Sara as the subject and the past perfect. Start with “Sara said”.
acceptedAnswers: Sara said she had completed the course.
Sara said that she had completed the course.
speakingExercises.feedback: Had completed places the course completion before Sara’s statement was reported.

speakingExercises.prompt: In the morning, Ben said, “I will call the supplier.” Later, tell a colleague what he said. Begin “Ben said” and use would.
acceptedAnswers: Ben said he would call the supplier.
Ben said that he would call the supplier.
speakingExercises.feedback: Would backshifts Ben’s earlier use of will.

speakingExercises.prompt: Adele told you, “I can meet you on Friday.” Report the message, calling the listener me. Begin “Adele said” and use could.
acceptedAnswers: Adele said she could meet me on Friday.
Adele said that she could meet me on Friday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Could reports can, while you changes to me from the listener’s perspective.

speakingExercises.prompt: Martin said, “I lost the keys last night.” Report this in one sentence beginning “Martin said”, using the past perfect for lost. Keep last night.
acceptedAnswers: Martin said he had lost the keys last night.
Martin said that he had lost the keys last night.
speakingExercises.feedback: Had lost is one acceptable way to report an earlier past simple event.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make exactly two sentences. First report Nina’s words “I am tired” with past-tense backshift. Second report “I have finished my shift” using the past perfect. Begin both sentences “Nina said”.
acceptedAnswers: Nina said she was tired. Nina said she had finished her shift.
Nina said that she was tired. Nina said that she had finished her shift.
Nina said that she was tired. Nina said she had finished her shift.
Nina said she was tired. Nina said that she had finished her shift.
speakingExercises.feedback: Was tired reports the earlier state; had finished reports a completed action.

speakingExercises.prompt: Owen said to Maya, “I will share my notes with you.” Maya reports his promise to a friend. Begin “Owen said” and finish with “with me”. Use would.
acceptedAnswers: Owen said he would share his notes with me.
Owen said that he would share his notes with me.
speakingExercises.feedback: Change I to he, my to his, and you to me while backshifting will to would.

listeningExercises.audioText: At breakfast, Lin told us she was searching for an apartment, not buying one.
listeningExercises.prompt: What housing plan did Lin report?
choices: She was looking for an apartment.
She had already purchased a home.
She planned to sell her apartment.
listeningExercises.feedback: Was searching for an apartment rather than buying signals a search, not a purchase.

listeningExercises.audioText: Omar said he had booked the coach tickets the previous evening, so we did not need to buy them.
listeningExercises.prompt: When did Omar complete the booking?
listeningExercises.feedback: Had booked and the previous evening place the purchase before his report.

listeningExercises.audioText: Iris said she would collect the parcel after work.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word modal verb phrase immediately after “she”.
acceptedAnswers: would collect
listeningExercises.feedback: Would collect is audible and reports a future action from an earlier viewpoint.

listeningExercises.audioText: Renee said she could repair the lamp, but she could not find her tools.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why had Renee not repaired the lamp yet?
choices: She lacked the ability to repair it.
The lamp had already been repaired.
She could not find her tools.
listeningExercises.feedback: Could repair expresses ability; the obstacle is that her tools are missing.

listeningExercises.audioText: The director said the team was testing the software during the morning, not presenting it to clients.
listeningExercises.prompt: What was the team doing that morning?
listeningExercises.feedback: Was testing describes the reported ongoing activity, contrasted with presenting.

listeningExercises.audioText: Sofia said her brother had already left for the station when she called him.
choices: Her brother left for the station.
They arrived at the station together.
listeningExercises.feedback: Had already left places the departure before Sofia’s call.

listeningExercises.audioText: The guide said the museum was closing early that afternoon.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word past-continuous phrase immediately after “museum”.
acceptedAnswers: was closing
listeningExercises.feedback: Was closing backshifts an ongoing or arranged action to a past reporting viewpoint.

listeningExercises.audioText: Jamie said he had forgotten the access code before the meeting.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word perfect verb phrase immediately after “he”.
acceptedAnswers: had forgotten
listeningExercises.feedback: Had forgotten shows that forgetting preceded the later report.
